# Owned synthetic INIT stream

`guest.s` and `link.ld` are the entire guest source. GNU Binutils 2.44
(`bfin-elf`, `-mcpu=bf524`) supplies the assembler and linker; there is no C
compiler, runtime, vendor source, firmware, OTP or WAD input. The existing
`blackfin-fixture` CI job rebuilds every image and checks the source/image/symbol
manifest. Committed `.ldr` files allow native tests without a Blackfin toolchain.

```sh
python3 tests/fixtures/init_handoff/build.py \
  --as "$BFIN_AS" --ld "$BFIN_LD" --output build/init-rebuild --check
```

Use the already available GNU 2.44 executables for those two variables. No new
toolchain installation is needed. `--update` is an explicit maintainer action
that replaces only these synthetic fixture files and their manifest. The build
receipt in the output directory records executable hashes, versions and exact
commands. The manifest records portable toolchain identity, all source hashes,
image hashes, symbols and the shared MAIN payload hash.

The outer image uses the ordinary direct loader to install a small guest caller
and a nested stream in L1 data RAM. That caller sets a scratchpad stack and enters
the existing embedded ROM through the documented `BFROM_MEMBOOT` API. The ROM
loads INIT code, clears a previously dirtied mailbox word with zero fill, processes a zero-payload INIT marker,
passes live boot data in R0, and calls the guest INIT. INIT installs its callback
and changes the active source by 16 bytes. Without this change the ROM reaches a
poison FIRST/FINAL header and the guest publishes error E004. With it, the ROM
loads MAIN, calls the guest callback and transfers through EVT1.

This is **memory boot**. The backing NAND generated by `build.py` is a 4,096-byte
public arithmetic pattern, opened by the real snapshot backend in every run. It
is not a boot-area image. Both comparison paths retain that same backend and
issue zero NAND commands. NAND boot, ECC, block skipping, OTP/preboot and the
physical TE-BOOT 2.30 handoff are unqualified. No raw NAND or OTP file is committed.
The guest's `dUserLong` points to its own context, not an invented NAND structure.

The MAIN section is byte-identical in every image. `direct.ldr` loads it with the
existing direct loader and never runs INIT or the callback. `stream.ldr` contains
the inner stream: attempting to run its first DXE directly fails the live-data
check. Other images deliberately corrupt the callback context, omit SDRAM setup,
ignore redirection, remove the INIT marker or zero fill, or supply null, misaligned or aligned
but malformed boot data. These are independent synthetic controls; no existing
firmware image or admission check is modified.

The code requests a synthetic enabled bank and refresh value, writes/reads a
sentinel, changes SIC wake masks and SYSCFG, and transforms one loaded word in the
callback. These are functional register/memory tests. They do not qualify SDRAM
power-up, electrical timing, cache/CPLB coherency, PLL relock or physical clocks.
See [the validation and execution contract](../../../docs/init-handoff.md).
